Create the FULL-PICTURE version. Recompose onto a TRUE WIDE LANDSCAPE 16:9 canvas, target 2880x1620. The input is a squarish 3:2 layout and feels horizontally squeezed. This is a layout refinement, NOT a horizontal pixel stretch: preserve natural proportions of people, notebooks, robot, lettering and circles. Spread the content across more horizontal room and increase gaps around arrows and groups. Use nearly the full available width with consistent ~3% safe margins. Do not leave broad unused side gutters that recreate the narrow feeling. The expanded layout should look like our other wide technical illustrations.
Keep exact title "GitHub Manager: RAG in practice", exact subtitle "Fixed, single-pass retrieval-augmented classification", and descriptor "Sparse label retrieval + durable application memory". Preserve the names "Evidence Parser", "Canonical Retriever", "TF-IDF + alias boost", "E0: metadata", "E1+: README passages", "Compact evidence", "RAKE phrases", "Candidate definitions", "User JSON", "System prompt", "Output schema", "Then validate & review".
Keep BOTH bands from the supplied full picture:
TOP, a subordinate band headed "Earlier: build the canonical registry". Repository collection "Metadata + README" -> local "Evidence Parser" and separate "RAKE" extraction -> "Collection evidence + phrases" booklet -> "Taxonomy LLM" and "Draft" -> human "Review & publish" -> "Canonical registry". Registry contents "IDs · kinds · names · definitions · aliases", with independent Domain/Project/Topic/Tag tabs and note "Approved vocabulary · reused below". Keep this earlier prerequisite distinct from classification, not an additional call per repository. Source examples may be shortened to avoid dense paragraphs, but preserve every named operation and authority boundary. Do not turn the earlier band into a dense series of generic boxes.
BOTTOM, the dominant retrieval/augmentation/generation flow as specified below. Its lower registry is labeled "Canonical registry (same approved vocabulary)".
The classification path has three dominant areas "1 Retrieval", "2 Augment", "3 Generate". Make the retrieval area the widest, roughly 48% of the main row, augmentation roughly 27%, generation roughly 25%, with usable white space between them.
Retrieval contains A, "Source evidence selection": "Metadata + README" documents -> "Evidence Parser" (local passage selection) -> a shared retained-evidence stack with "E0: metadata" and "E1+: README passages". The retained evidence has three distinct uses: a local compact-selection route to "Compact evidence"; separate "RAKE" phrase extraction to "RAKE phrases"; and an explicitly arrowheaded query route labeled "All retained evidence (query)" into the Canonical Retriever. This query MUST originate before compaction and MUST NOT come from the RAKE phrase list.
Retrieval also contains B, "Canonical label lookup": an approved canonical registry notebook -> a magnifying glass named "Canonical Retriever", captioned "TF-IDF + alias boost"; the retained-evidence query is its SECOND explicit incoming source. Lookup produces "Candidate definitions" cards marked "Project", "Topic", "Tag". The registry itself contains Domain/Project/Topic/Tag, but only these three kinds become classification candidates. Do not send the full registry directly to the LLM.
Augment has an open "User JSON" request booklet. Three separate clear incoming routes terminate at corresponding inserts: "Compact evidence", "RAKE phrases", "Candidate definitions". Separate tabs read "System prompt" and "Output schema". Keep routes clean and labeled, without crossings. The model receives BOTH source evidence and shortlisted definitions, not only candidates.
Generate has a small friendly "LLM" robot -> paper "Classification" with schematic headings "Canonical IDs", "Evidence IDs", "Confidence + reason". No fabricated values. Beneath it a small clipboard and human reviewer "Then validate & review", with "Schema + ID checks", "Evidence IDs exist", "Review suggestions". Valid evidence IDs are not depicted as proof of semantic correctness.
A modest low-height footer reads "Saved application state: profiles · taxonomy · decisions · receipts", with a few small flat papers if helpful, not furniture. No agentic search loop, dense vector icons, neural reranker or fake metrics.
